editorial:
You meet five former special ops guys who are tired of scraping by after years of service. When one of them finds a chance to steal seventy-five million dollars from a drug lord in South America, the old team gets back together. The plan sounds simple at first, but greed, guilt, and bad choices quickly turn a clean job into a messy survival mission. The movie has a gritty, tense feel, with jungle heat, heavy bags of cash, and constant pressure from every direction. You can feel the bond between these men, but also the cracks that money brings out.

The cast, including Ben Affleck, Oscar Isaac, and Charlie Hunnam, sells the tired-soldier energy well, and the action scenes feel grounded instead of flashy. The pacing starts slow, then turns into a tense chase with real consequences. On the downside, some characters feel thin, and the story can get heavy. If you like military heist thrillers with moral gray areas, this is a solid pick.
endingExplained: In the final stretch, the overloaded helicopter crashes in the mountains, forcing the men to carry the cash on foot. Greed and stress push the group apart, leading to violence, lost money, and deaths. The survivors eventually reach a village and give away much of what remains to the family of a man killed during the escape. They leave with far less money than planned, realizing the heist cost them more than it gave.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves military heist thrillers with moral gray areas.
